title: A fixed June 2018 OI SST v2 step fit is larger at 0-120 E than elsewhere at 40-60 S
abstract: We tested the date and spatial structure of a reported 2018 Southern Ocean OI SST v2 change. Monthly 2001-2022 data at 40-60 S were compared with ERSSTv5 and COBE-SST2 on fixed masks. We searched 192 dates with seasonal terms, polynomial drift and block-bootstrap calibration. ERSST selected June 2018, but the search p value rose from 0.0055 with linear drift to 0.1085 with cubic drift. COBE selected February 2014 with curved drift. A test that swapped longitude sectors and references succeeded in only one direction. An exploratory fixed June 2018 test found that 0-120 E carried 69-76 percent of the quadratic full-band step on 31 percent of the area. The steps there were -0.320 and -0.233 C against the two references. Outside that region they were -0.045 and -0.047 C, with intervals that included zero. The spatial contrasts stayed negative with quadratic and cubic drift on a warmer mask. This gives a target for a source audit, but does not establish one common step across the Southern Ocean. Region selection, shared source errors, residual dependence and one-step models limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, figures, exact source hashes and retrieval instructions are included. Raw data and monthly extracts remain external.

display.caption: Fixed June 2018 quadratic difference fits at 40-60 S, 2001-2022. The region split was selected after the date scans. Intervals are pointwise and conditional.
Date scans and transition-width fits show dependence on reference and model. Sector best dates are descriptive.

citations.reason: We test the spatial structure and date stability of its OI v2 feature with new raw-file analysis. Observations overlap.
Its AMIP source-transfer result motivates a spatial audit. We use its source-file provenance to locate existing shared data, not its monthly extracts.
Correction uncertainty motivates sensitivity tests; we do not reuse its data or code.
